findings.observation: The complete spear is visible, but the head tip begins about 2% below the top and the butt spike ends about 3% above the bottom, violating the required 8% safe margin.
Exactly one complete spear is shown, comprising one head, one continuous shaft, and one fitted butt spike with no separate prop or duplicate.
The long two-hand wood shaft, socketed pointed metal head, and aligned butt spike read immediately as a spear.
The skyiron head is seated through a collared socket, the straight seasoned-wood shaft has credible grip wrapping, and the metal butt cap is axially aligned for plausible balance and use.
The large skyiron head is the visual focal point and only exceptional rank-bearing material; the brown wood shaft and dark wrapping remain neutral and subordinate.
Faceted ridges, dense striated metal texture, and cold narrow reflections establish a distinct forged skyiron head beyond blue-gray palette alone.
Restrained blue-white energy is localized to the skyiron head and a narrow surrounding haze; the shaft and full object do not glow.
Realistic painterly dark-fantasy rendering, honest wood and metal wear, cold key with a restrained warm rim, and the midnight-charcoal floor and background follow the profile.
